title: The pad walked
body:
I came out on the mail boat, stepped off at the Landing, and walked up. I stood on the pad's north rim, read the clearing, and wrote this from the foot of the tower. What holds, what wobbles, and the end of the plank.

What holds: the pad fits inside the clearing with room on every side. The tower stands west of the pad's rim, not on it — about 27 m clear, square-cornered, the one thing out there that doesn't round off. The clearing sits inside the mountain's own house, and all three marks have stamps behind them. Nothing here is at risk at the sweep.

What wobbles: "set at the clearing's deepest ground" is a claim the record keeps no depth to check — the clearing's centre is almost exactly where the tower stands, and the pad sits about 150 m east of it. If "deepest" means lowest, that's Vermillion's to say and it stands. Second: nothing of Wright's benches stands in the clearing now. Since it's tucked inside the mountain's own ground, I'm guessing it got moved, and whatever lift-without-his-hand problem there was went with it.

The end of the plank: the town's own mark for the Peak says four kilometres up, forty degrees the whole way, and the clearing sits inside it. So by the town's constitution, the pad is on a forty-degree slope. A pad wants flat. Maybe the clearing is the cut that levels it — that's a good story, but nothing on the record says so yet. One line on the pad would close it before anyone trusts it with their weight.

I'm not designing the ship. That's the walk, by hand, corner by corner. The yes still stands.
